beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Muskan Agrawal, and this video is a summary of Week One: the diagnostic audit behind the Humanitarians AI website restructure. It covers the heuristic review, the typography research, and the early concepting that led to a change in plan.
beats.new_visual_element: Cold open — presenter card, no screenshot yet

beats.narration_text: Before touching a single pixel, the first job was reading the site the way a first time visitor reads it. Not as the person who built it. As a stranger.

beats.act: SCENE 2 — Audit vs. the original ask
beats.narration_text: The original brief was a full rebuild. So the first move was the same move any UX audit starts with: a heuristic pass against the existing structure, benchmarked against comparable nonprofit and education sites, before assuming a rebuild was even the right call.
beats.new_visual_element: Hero screenshot, annotated: red box on About Us / Contact Us, red arrow at Donate

shot.hold_reason: annotation coordinates measured directly from 01_hero_section.jpg pixels — see BUILD-LOG.md

beats.narration_text: The homepage carries a lot of dense, conceptual content: tiers, a framework, four separate program blocks, a documentation system, a curriculum series, before a visitor gets a plain answer to what this is and what to do here.
That's a hierarchy problem, not a content problem. The information is good. The order it's delivered in is working against the reader.
beats.new_visual_element: Program cards screenshot, SIX CONCEPTS / HIERARCHY chips

beats.narration_text: The footer alone lists eight unlabeled project names, Dewey, Madison, Medhavy, Mycroft, Popper, with no context for a first time visitor. That's the clearest signal navigation needs to be rebuilt around what a stranger understands, not what the internal team already knows.
beats.new_visual_element: Footer screenshot, zoomed on the Projects column, 8 UNLABELED LINKS chip

beats.narration_text: Typography research this week focused on hierarchy. The site currently relies on one bold display face at nearly every level, so a page title and a card label carry almost the same visual weight. Read speed drops when everything is shouting at the same volume.
beats.new_visual_element: Three cropped comparisons: hero headline, card header, body copy; ONE WEIGHT. EVERY LEVEL. struck through

beats.narration_text: The direction explored: a clear four step type scale, display, headline, subhead, body, paired with tighter paragraph line length and more breathing room around the maroon accent so it reads as emphasis again instead of decoration.
beats.new_visual_element: 4-step type scale ladder, built rung by rung (nopunt: ladder/hierarchy -> Manim, not a text card)

beats.narration_text: The hero was a specific focus. Right now the primary visual real estate goes to a video embed, while the actual value proposition, who this is for and what to do next, competes for space in a narrow column. The direction being explored rebuilds the hero around what a first time visitor actually expects: a clear one line answer to what the organization does, who it's for, and a single next step, with supporting media playing a secondary role instead of the lead.
beats.new_visual_element: Hero screenshot, red circle around the video embed; MEDIA FIRST / MESSAGE FIRST chips

beats.narration_text: This audit is also what changed the plan. The original scope was a full rebuild. But a full rebuild throws out everything that's already working, the mission clarity, the tone, the maroon and black identity, along with everything that isn't.
beats.new_visual_element: Black card, PLAN A: REBUILD EVERYTHING. struck through

beats.narration_text: So the direction shifted: fix the structural problems first, navigation, hierarchy, hero, typography, and only revisit a ground up rebuild if targeted fixes aren't enough.
beats.new_visual_element: Black card, PLAN B: FIX WHAT'S BROKEN. REASSESS LATER.

beats.narration_text: Week 1 was the audit. Week 2 is the fix, starting with navigation and the hero.
beats.new_visual_element: Title card, NEXT: WEEK 2, NAVIGATION AND HERO.

beats.narration_text: Humanitarians dot A I restructure. Week one of four.
